purpose: ONE deterministic 0-10 overall-destination score for every published record with enough evidence. verified and estimated are PROVENANCE/confidence states over this SAME formula — never different formulas on one scale. Measures overall destination VALUE, not seasonal suitability (a highly seasonal destination must not be penalized for having one ideal season).

states.verified: rubric value whose inputs were editorially verified against authoritative sources (score-specific provenance: verification date + source URLs, committed in kai-89-score-verification-ledger.json). NEVER derived from generic ratingMetadata.confidence.
states.estimated: rubric value over catalogue fields with model provenance (sourceClass model). Visibly labeled estimated; never presented as editorial.
states.unavailable: weighted evidence coverage below the threshold. Localized unavailable state, value null; never a neutral-5 estimate, never a legacy rating, never another field.

evidenceThresholdRationale: coverage = sum of weights of dimensions with DIRECT evidence. 0.5 = at least half of the rubric weight backed by evidence — equivalently SIGNIFICANCE plus any secondary dimension, or RECOGNITION plus RICHNESS. A single sparse dimension (e.g. importance alone = 0.40) is not enough: a lack of evidence is not evidence of average quality.
computedAt: runtime (computeOverallScore in src/shared/services/recommendation/scoreRubric.ts); persisted per record by the generator
neverUses: legacy ratings vector (ratings.*) — a separate evidence family with its own confidence gating (ratingMetadata)
season vector (seasonal suitability is a separate dimension, never an overall score)

officialWebsite / status / fieldSources / highlight count / visit-window presence / walking-data presence (catalogue-completeness proxies; evidence maturity belongs to confidence/provenance, not the numeric value)

dimensions.scoring: importance tier: major 9 / notable 7 / standard 5 / minor 3. No designation bonuses — external designations are credited ONLY in RECOGNITION (anti-double-counting).
dimensions.rationale: A destination's national/international standing is the primary driver of overall value for a traveller deciding what to see.
dimensions.evidence: importance present and in the tier map

dimensions.scoring: highest designation tier wins (single credit, never stacked): UNESCO (collection unesco-japan or unesco/world-heritage tag) 9; national park / quasi-national park / Japan heritage / national treasure / top-100 castle / three-great (collections national-parks-japan, quasi-national-parks-japan, japan-top-castles, original-12-castles or matching tags) 7; any other collection membership or prefectural/registered/historic-site tag 6; tags present without designation 4 (absence of designation is evidence of absence).
dimensions.rationale: Third-party designations (UNESCO, national parks, heritage programmes) are independent recognition of quality.

dimensions.scoring: distinct category count >=4 -> 8, 2-3 -> 6, 1 -> 4; +0.5 when indoorPercent 20-80 (balanced indoor/outdoor). Highlight count NEVER changes the value (evidence maturity only).
dimensions.rationale: Depth and variety of things to see/do is a core value dimension; extreme single-focus or single-environment places are lower.
dimensions.evidence: categories non-empty OR highlights non-empty OR indoorPercent present

dimensions.scoring: finite transport-mode count >=3 -> 8, 1-2 -> 6. visit-window and walking data NEVER change the value (provenance signals only).
dimensions.rationale: A destination a traveller can actually reach is worth more; pure accessibility, low weight.
dimensions.evidence: at least one finite transport mode

composite: value = round( sum(covered_dimension_value * weight) / sum(covered_weights) ) to 1 decimal; clamp 1-10. Uncovered dimensions contribute NEITHER numerator NOR denominator — a missing input never manufactures a neutral 5.
missingCompositeBehavior: if weighted evidence coverage < 0.5 the record is unavailable (value null). No neutral-5 fallback, no automatic estimate.
antiDoubleCounting: a designation is credited in exactly ONE dimension (RECOGNITION). SIGNIFICANCE reads ONLY the catalogue importance field; importance and external designations are disjoint inputs. Multiple designations within RECOGNITION credit the highest tier once (never stacked).
catalogueCompletenessGuard: officialWebsite, status, fieldSources, highlight count, recommendedVisitHours presence and walkingMin presence are evidence-maturity signals: they may affect confidence/provenance reporting but NEVER the numeric value.
versioning: bump rubricVersion on any input/weight/scoring/threshold change; the basis note in persisted scoreMetadata and the score-state audit must reference this version.
